articles.title_orig: Fed meeting recap: Warsh says central bank will host fewer rate-setting meetings in future years
articles.title_zh: Fed meeting recap: Warsh says central bank will host fewer rate-setting meetings in future years
articles.content_orig:
The Federal Reserve held steady on rates at the conclusion of its October meeting, maintaining its target range of 3.75% to 4%.
Two members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented from the decision: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack were in favor of raising rates by a quarter percentage point.
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh announced that the central bank will reduce the number of rate-setting meetings starting in 2027, noting that while eight meetings per year is "the right number" for the FOMC, one of them will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy starting in 2027. The remainder will be policy-setting meetings.
In 2028, the Fed will plan to host two meetings focused on strategy discussions and the remaining six will be centered on policy setting, Warsh said.
Inflation remains hot, the economy is strong — and that means the Federal Reserve should be lifting rates, according to bond investor Jeffrey Gundlach.
"I think the Fed should be raising interest rates, based upon the 2-year Treasury being at 4 and three-quarters percent, and now the yield curve in the wake of this news conference is steepening again," Gundlach, CEO and Chief Investment Officer of DoubleLine Capital, said on CNBC's "Closing Bell" after Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh wrapped up his news conference.
The 2-year Treasury yield , which is sensitive to Fed policy, was last trading at 4.714%.
At the Fed's press conference, which came after central bank policymakers opted to hold rates steady at a range of 3.75% and 4%, Warsh highlighted the strength of the economy.
"Broadly, what I heard in the room the last couple of days is consistent with my own views, which is the economy is strong," the central bank leader said.
Gundlach noted that it's not clear why the Fed is holding steady on rates.
"What are you waiting for? You just upgraded the economy right here," he said, referring to Warsh's comments at the press conference.
Read more from CNBC's Davis Giangiulio on Gundlach's comments here.
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh repeated again in his Wednesday press conference that he does not favor the Federal Reserve signaling the future path of interest rates and monetary policy in a process known colloquially as "forward guidance."
"I don't believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis," Warsh told reporter after the Fed kept its benchmark fed funds rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4%.
"I have to give that caveat because in the darkest days of the 2008 financial crisis, in part using some literature and thinking from a very recent Nobel Prize winner, that kind of forward guidance is actually quite helpful. But in normal, ordinary times, especially times where the underlying deal economy is this strong, I don't believe in it. I don't favor it."
— Scott Schnipper, Fred Imbert
Warsh said higher interest rates have had an effect on the artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out.
"Interest rates have had an effect," Warsh said. "You see market participants that are discriminating between the kinds of investments they want to make. You've seen credit spreads for certain assets widen out, gap out. For others, you've seen some tightening in financial conditions, but not significantly.
"I don't believe that they're somehow divorced from the rest of the economy," he added.
Warsh said the capital expenditure story is "not just strong, but it is broadening." He said it's "much harder" to argue that economic strength is driven by a a small group of sectors today than it was several quarters prior.
The public will be hearing less from the Federal Reserve when it comes to interest rate decisions.
Warsh announced Wednesday that the central bank will alter its meeting schedule in coming years, seemingly part of his plans to pare back the impact that he and his colleagues have on financial markets.
Under the details Warsh revealed, the Federal Open Market Committee will still meet eight times a year.
However, unlike the current system in which the panel votes on where it will set its benchmark interest rate, one of those meetings in 2027 will focus solely on strategy. In 2028, there will be two strategy sessions.
"We believe eight meetings per year is the right number for the FOMC," Warsh said, but noted the committee doesn't need to vote at each one.
"What's the reasoning behind this change? To me, it's quite straightforward," he added. "Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular, and information-rich intervals.
"But it's equally important we reserve time and space as an intellectually diverse group for strategic deliberations, for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons, focusing, as I say, on the left side of the decimal point."
Warsh has emphasized the importance of "regime change" at the Fed, a process that has entailed the establishment of multiple task forces aimed at looking at how the central bank operates. One such task force will address communication issues.
The meeting change appears to be a first step in the process of changing the Fed's approach.
"I believe the setting of the meeting schedule and agenda is more than some administrative detail. It's an institutional choice, affecting the nature and the quality of our deliberations, and ultimately the wisdom of our decisions," he said. "It's yet another change to get the conduct of monetary policy on the right track."
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said politics did not influence Wednesday's decision to maintain rates.
"I just spent two days with my colleagues upstairs. I didn't hear an utterance about politics. I didn't hear a reference to politics, elections, what's happening in the next week or so," Warsh said. Midterm elections are scheduled for Nov. 3.
"Didn't hear anything about it, and I don't believe it had any role in the decision, not just for me, but my colleagues around the room," he said.
At these policy meetings that will specifically focus on broad strategy, Warsh said he doesn't anticipate that the Fed will make a rate decision or release a statement.
He then said "it's not obvious yet" what the Fed would share following these meetings.
"There's more news to come on that," Warsh said. "The decision on the new format for the meetings is relatively new."
Warsh said there was a "robust discussion" on how to handle these meetings over a few gatherings.
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said economic growth has been positive after the agency maintained rates at its October meeting, keeping rates at a range between 3.75% and 4%.
"Economic growth has strengthened. The GDP increase in the first half of this year was revised up from an earlier estimate of 1.8 percent up to 2.4 percent, and the third quarter appears to have brought an even more rapid advance," Warsh said.
Warsh said the Fed's discussion over recent days "focused mainly on the price stability side of our remit."
He said the full employment side of its dual mandate has been "quite positive," citing a decreasing jobless rate compared with a year ago. Warsh also noted that the unemployment insurance claims volume, when looking at a four-week average, is at "the lowest level in generations."
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said the central bank will cut back on the number of meetings where members vote on rates. Said Warsh: "We believe eight meetings per year is the right number for the FOMC, but in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated. The rest will be regular FOMC policy setting meetings, and I expect that in 2028 we'll have two meetings dedicated discussions of strategy and six for setting policy."
Later Warsh added that he doesn't "anticipate" making a policy decision during these strategy meetings.

articles.title_orig: Trump says US will beat China in AI as technology emerges
articles.title_zh: Trump says US will beat China in AI as technology emerges
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Artificial intelligence has emerged as the critical sticking point between the U.S. and China. President Donald Trump, who has named it “super intelligence,” insists the U.S. will beat China in the AI competition.
Trump said while campaigning for president that tariffs would form the crux of the bilateral relationship. The U.S. and China, the world’s two largest economies, have been engaged in a trade war during both of Trump’s terms.
Speaking Sept. 13 in Ireland, Trump said the U.S. is leading China in AI.
“We’re leading China in AI, we’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump said.
During a state visit to Beijing in May, Trump praised Chinese President Xi Jinping.
“And it’s to me an honor. We’ve had a fantastic relationship. We’ve gotten along. When they were difficulties, we worked it out,” Trump said.
Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September for a state visit. He touted what he called “the tremendous strides” he and Xi had already made on national security, trade and technology.
At the summit, the U.S. and China agreed to extend a trade truce until January. No agreement was reached on implementing safeguards for AI.
Trump and Xi are set to meet again in China next month.

articles.title_orig: Trump admin sues Utah to save Kalshi from the state's total ban on gambling
articles.title_zh: Trump admin sues Utah to save Kalshi from the state's total ban on gambling
articles.content_orig:
The Trump administration is trying to stop Utah from enforcing its gambling ban against Kalshi, making Utah the 10th state sued by the US government agency that regulates prediction markets.
Utah, which prohibits gambling, sued Kalshi in a state court last week. Utah’s lawsuit seeks an order prohibiting Kalshi from offering bets on sports, elections, politics, and other events.
“Kalshi runs an online casino in Utah and calls it a prediction market. That violates Utah law,” Utah Attorney General Derek Brown, a Republican, said last week. “Not only do our state laws ban gambling but Utah is one of only two states where gambling is also prohibited under the state constitution. For 130 years, Utah has been clear: gambling has no place here, and we will enforce our laws.”
Utah already defeated Kalshi in federal court after the prediction market filed a preemptive lawsuit that sought to prevent the state from enforcing its gambling laws. Now that Utah is moving ahead in its attempt to shut down Kalshi, it must defend against a lawsuit filed by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).
The CFTC “has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws,” the commission said yesterday . “The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law.”
If Utah can shut down Kalshi, that could spell trouble for Kalshi’s chief prediction-market rival, Polymarket, and for sports betting sites like DraftKings and FanDuel. DraftKings and FanDuel advertise availability in all US states via a mix of products , including prediction-market platforms in states like Utah. Both are registered with the CFTC.
The Utah attorney general’s office declined to comment today on the CFTC lawsuit. The CFTC previously filed lawsuits against Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin. The federal agency also filed briefs supporting Kalshi in appeals court cases.
“Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.”
The US Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) gives the CFTC authority to regulate swaps. The key legal questions being grappled with by courts throughout the US are whether event contracts offered by prediction markets qualify as swaps, and whether the CFTC jurisdiction over swaps preempts states from applying their gambling laws.
The CFTC is suing Utah in the same US district court that previously ruled in Utah’s favor. Kalshi sued Utah in February in an attempt to stop the state from bringing an enforcement action against the prediction market.
In August, US District Judge Robert Shelby granted Utah’s motion for summary judgment and denied Kalshi’s motion for a preliminary injunction. Shelby wrote , “[T]he court concludes the federal law relied upon by Kalshi does not preempt Utah’s ability to enforce its anti-gambling laws.”
Shelby determined the text of US law makes it clear that state regulation is not forbidden. US law states that CFTC jurisdiction does not “supersede or limit the jurisdiction conferred on courts of the United States or any State,” and “explicitly provides for State regulation of its gaming laws in all but a few specified cases,” he wrote.
“Congress is aware that some States permit gambling while others do not, and the CEA explicitly provides for State jurisdiction,” Shelby wrote.
Kalshi is now appealing its loss to the US Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit but was unable to obtain an injunction preventing enforcement of the state gambling ban while that litigation continues. On September 8, Tenth Circuit judges denied Kalshi’s emergency motion for an injunction pending appeal. Utah filed its lawsuit seeking a shutdown of Kalshi about six weeks later.
The CFTC lawsuit against Utah makes arguments similar to the ones already rejected by the district court, although some other courts have ruled otherwise.
“Utah is not the first State that has attempted to invade the Commission’s exclusive jurisdiction over swaps,” the CFTC lawsuit said. “Already, several federal courts—including the Third Circuit—have swiftly responded by issuing or affirming temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions barring the States from enforcing their gambling laws against CFTC-regulated exchanges that offer sports-related or other event contracts.”
The Third Circuit appeals court ruled that New Jersey cannot regulate sports bets on prediction markets. But Kalshi lost similar cases in the Sixth Circuit and Ninth Circuit in rulings that went in favor of Ohio, Tennessee, and Nevada.
Because circuit appeals courts are divided on the issue, it is likely that the Supreme Court will take up the case and determine whether states can apply their gambling laws to prediction markets. New Jersey petitioned the Supreme Court to resolve the circuit split, and 39 other states and the District of Columbia filed a brief supporting New Jersey’s petition.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk is a 'real genius', Putin says after satellite talks with SpaceX boss
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk is a 'real genius', Putin says after satellite talks with SpaceX boss
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk is a "real genius", Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday after revealing the two are in "close" contact about satellite technology.
The remarks came during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, during which Putin discussed Russia's own satellite internet project Rassvet, which provides internet connections to people from satellites.
"He's a genius, a real genius," Putin said of Musk, according to a translation of his remarks by the BBC. "We are in close contact with our American partners, including Mr. Musk."
Starlink is part of Musk's company SpaceX. The company did not respond to a request for comment.
Putin added that it was important for Russia to be in contact with Musk so Rassvet and Starlink satellites do not "interfere with each other in orbit".
"We and our American partners value this mutually, and despite all the political questions, we are working hard," he said.
Starlink has launched roughly 13,000 of its satellites, according to the company. By contrast there are only a couple of dozen Rassvet satellites currently in orbit, according to online satellite trackers.
The Russian Embassy in South Africa said on Wednesday Rassvet is "Russia's Starlink alternative" and "marks only the country's first steps in this field".
"Russia maintains close contacts with the US on space, including with Elon Musk," the embassy wrote.
Putin's comments about Rassvet and Starlink were made as the US and Russia appear to be growing closer, even as it approaches five years since Putin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Ukraine relied on Starlink internet in its efforts to keep Russia's forces at bay. But its military last week suddenly suffered Starlink connectivity problems, something Musk has admitted SpaceX did intentionally.
US President Donald Trump earlier this month said he'd struck a deal with Russia to import diesel in an effort to lower gas prices that have skyrocketed due to the US war with Iran.
Then Trump waived certain sanctions against Russia that were set to take effect.
Not long after, a US citizen was released from Russian custody, with US envoy Steve Witkoff referring to Putin as a "humanitarian".
Musk was born in South Africa and then immigrated to Canada before settling in the US. All of his business ventures, including Tesla, SpaceX and Starlink, are based in America, with most operating out of California and Texas.
The billionaire, and off and on again trillionaire, has been one of the biggest political allies and financiers of Trump and other Republican US politicians.

articles.title_orig: AI Is Finding a Flood of Bugs, and Silicon Valley Is Rushing to Fix Them
articles.title_zh: AI Is Finding a Flood of Bugs, and Silicon Valley Is Rushing to Fix Them
articles.content_orig:
In July 2004, security researcher Stefan Esser sent a warning .
A critical flaw in PHP , the programming language that powers 70% of the world’s websites, could allow an attacker to do some seriously nefarious stuff: read passwords, steal databases or even take over entire websites.
But Esser’s warning went mostly ignored for decades. In 2020, another researcher discovered a related problem, and the PHP overseers issued a partial fix. A similar PHP vulnerability was uncovered in 2024 – but was left unfixed.
Why was one of the most severe threats to the foundation of the internet left unresolved for 22 years?
Because it would have taken mind-numbing work for a human to figure out how to take advantage of it: tedious, time-consuming, monotonous coding. That rendered the PHP vulnerability impractical to exploit.
AI just figured out how to do it in two days.
On Wednesday, OpenAI’s public revelation of the exploit was announced in conjunction with a security update to fix the problem.
Why AI agents keep breaking loose
Phew, you might think. The good guys got to it first. But the AI-assisted discovery deeply concerned cybersecurity researchers, because the next one might come from someone who wants to weaponize it.
And AI doesn’t care who’s pulling the trigger.
The internet is held together with shoestring and bubblegum.
An apt xkcd cartoon visualizes “all modern digital infrastructure” as a giant Jenga tower supported by one, thin, vertical block with the label: “a project some random person in Nebraska has been thanklessly maintaining since 2003.”
On July 30, researchers at AI security company Calif, in conjunction with OpenAI’s new Patch the Planet security initiative, decided to point a large-language AI model at one of those Jenga blocks – PHP – and see what came of it. It didn’t expect to find anything critical.
On August 1, it found a method to attack PHP’s vulnerabilities . Days later, it found another. Then another. Later that month, Google-backed security company Wiz – another Patch the Planet participant – discovered new exploits for PHP vulnerabilities, too.
The patch went out Wednesday, and the companies publicly disclosed their findings. Wiz called it one of the most severe vulnerabilities in software history.
The security community lit up social media with I-told-you-sos.
“The security industry has long been warning about the coming security apocalypse, because AI can do these things very, very quickly – better than humans,” said Vyas Sekar, professor of computer engineering at Carnegie Mellon University. “This may be the first of many. This is a wakeup call.”
Sekar says there are more PHP-like vulnerabilities out there to discover and exploit. A lot more. Some are known, and many are unknown.
The wide availability of AI tools has significantly lowered the barrier to entry for hackers to take advantage of potential security vulnerabilities. That fact freaked out Anthropic enough that the AI company paused deployment of its Mythos model in June, as it was so good at exposing security vulnerabilities and finding vectors for attack that the US government labeled it a national security threat.
But Calif researcher Ryan Austin noted in a blog post that the company didn’t use any special AI models that weren’t generally available to the public.
That democratization of AI tools made clear that “security by exhaustion” is no longer a viable safeguard against bad guys, said Nick Rogers, CEO of Fieldwork AI.
For 22 years, PHP was like a bank with no security guards. Anyone could walk down to the vault and make off with the cash – if they had the time to try every code. It was such arduous work, it wasn’t worth anyone’s time.
But AI doesn’t get tired. And it can crack safes way faster than humans.
“Taking a theoretical (vulnerability) and proving you can exploit it is quite tedious and mechanical work,” said Rogers. “AI can keep churning until it figures it out. You don’t even need to try. You can drink coffee while it does it.”
Effectively, PHP is an engine that powers most of the internet. Until it was patched Wednesday, it had a fatal flaw.
A vulnerability left open a patch for an attacker to mess around with the way PHP processes requests to run websites. If a server crashed because it ran out of memory, it would leave stale data behind that could be exploited to leak the data or execute bad code.
Think of the exploit like taking advantage of a busy restaurant kitchen. Customers could overwhelm the chef with too many complex orders – so much that she quits midway through dinner, leaving dirty pans, raw ingredients and recipes strewn about the counter. Then, when a new chef is hired, he serves the contaminated food on filthy dishes – and even sends some recipes to customers along with their dinner orders.
Although the vulnerability was long known to be theoretically exploitable, figuring out how to do it proved exceedingly difficult. Hackers had to force the server into an out-of-memory crash at a specific instant to bypass PHP’s safety limits.
When researchers pointed AI at the problem, it quickly found a couple ways around that. One solution exploits a mismatch between the way PHP measures compressed files and decoded files. Effectively, it allowed compressed files through its gates, letting the file unpack itself and take over from the inside.
Another attacks PHP with deeply nested file structures that overwhelmed PHP’s directory structure, triggering the memory failure.
The vulnerability was patched, but the threat may not be over, noted Adam Meyers, vice president of counter adversary at security company CrowdStrike . Many outdated versions of PHP are still in use, and the patch almost certainly didn’t fix all of PHP’s problems.
Also, an apparent leak about the vulnerability before the patch was released resulted in thousands of exploits in the hours ahead of the announcement, according to security company Cloudflare .
“Bad guys don’t need to find the vulnerability first – they can weaponize it after the fact,” Meyers said. “We are still waiting to see how much of this shows up in the wild.”
OpenAI offered several suggestions in its disclosure about the PHP patch , all of which basically boil down to: Write better, more secure code from the start.
That’s not super helpful if your web application has been written using PHP.
“Migrating away from PHP is a pretty expensive process,” noted Meyers. “It’s not like switching from Microsoft mail to Google mail; you need to rebuild the whole application.”
If the solution isn’t to migrate 70% of the web to a new programming language, then fixing its underlying problems – and all the other software problems in the world – would hardly be an easy fix, either.
What’s needed, then, may be a paradigm shift in the way the security community operates. Effectively, assume everything poses a security risk.
Companies need to treat every single business operation like air traffic controllers treat their surroundings, said Madhu Shashanka, cofounder of security company Concentric AI.
“Everything is a potential vulnerability,” Shashanka said. “Every business operation is a high-stakes operation.”
For example, companies that leave certain software unpatched – even for a few days – are exposing themselves to vulnerabilities that are no longer too difficult or expensive for bad actors to exploit.
“Lots of vulnerabilities are out there that are never exploited because it takes effort,” said Shashanka. “AI has rendered that effort meaningless.”

articles.title_orig: Wendy’s, struggling with beef prices and growing competition, gets a buyout offer
articles.title_zh: Wendy’s, struggling with beef prices and growing competition, gets a buyout offer
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Wendy's ( WEN ) may be cooking up burgers for a billionaire soon.
Longtime Wendy's investor and former chairman Nelson Peltz of Trian Partners has reportedly offered $1.4 billion to buy the struggling fast food giant , according to an SEC filing.
Wendy's shares rose 15% in early trading. The company's market cap was $1.17 billion prior to the deal.
A Wendy's spokesperson didn't return a request for comment. A spokesperson for Trian Partners didn't return a request for comment.
Billionaire Peltz — while familiar with the operations — would essentially be buying a dumpster fire.
After nearly two years of struggles competing with the likes of behemoths McDonald's ( MCD ) and Yum! Brands' ( YUM ) Taco Bell, plus upstarts such as Shake Shack ( SHAK ), Wendy's is on the cusp of a large number of restaurant closures.
"With one of its largest franchisees filing bankruptcy in September (although contested by WEN given prior termination of franchise agreement), we think investors likely expect closures to tick higher than expected, but we admit visibility on our side remains somewhat limited and there could still be a range of outcomes," veteran restaurant analyst Andy Barish warned in a recent note.
"That said," he added, "given our view that there are likely additional franchise operators in the system facing challenges with leveraged balance sheets, higher interest rates and profitability pressures from higher beef, labor & build costs (like many others in QSR), we think it is prudent to moderate our development estimates and bake in more potential closures over the next 6-12 months, as the company works to strengthen its system."
Meritage Hospitality Group, one of Wendy's largest franchise operators, with more than 300 locations, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September following severe margin pressures and an escalating dispute with corporate headquarters. The company reportedly initiated plans to shutter at least 41 locations. Reports emerged this week that it could close up to 60.
The high-profile bankruptcy only added grease to the smoldering fire that is the Wendy's restaurant base.
Franchisees had already been closing their locations and heading for the hills.
Buried inside Wendy's brutal second quarter earnings call was a mention that 289 locations closed in the US during the first half of the year.
There are about 5,700 Wendy's in the US, and Barish estimated the Wendy's US store base will be around 5,600 by the end of 2027.
The decision on how many more locations will be closed falls on new CEO Bob Wright, who hasn't hidden his view that Wendy's needs to focus on more profitable locations.
Wright officially took over as CEO on May 21, adding to the yawning list of executive turnover at the fast food chain over the past two years. He is a seasoned fast food exec who spent the previous five years fixing Potbelly as CEO. Wright's appointment marked a return to Wendy's, where he previously served in several senior leadership roles, including COO.
Wright has his work cut out for him in saving Wendy's beyond tightening up the store base count.
Wendy's has posted six straight quarters of same-store sales declines, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace analysis.

articles.title_zh: Stock market today: Nasdaq wavers, S&P 500 and Dow climb as Fed votes to hold rates steady in 10-2 decision
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
US stocks edged higher on Wednesday as investors digested the Federal Reserve's 10-2 decision to hold interest rates steady and focus shifted to earnings results from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) and the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained roughly 0.2% and 0.3%, respectively. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) climbed roughly 0.3%
Investor attention turned toward the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, where the Fed voted to keep its funds rate unchanged , despite elevated inflation readings. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Fed Governor Lisa Cook dissented, favoring a rate hike.
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh also announced the central bank will have one less policy-setting meeting next year.
Sentiment in the tech trade has markedly improved this week, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting back-to-back gains. Semiconductor stocks rose for a third day in a row after South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix ( SKHY , 000660.KS ) reported a 632% year-over-year profit increase. Peeres Micron ( MU ) and Samsung ( 005930.KS ), also gained.
Oracle ( ORCL ) shares jumped after the software and cloud computing giant issued a fiscal 2030 revenue outlook of $225 billion, implying 35% annual growth.
Earnings season continues apace as two Big Tech giants and cloud leaders — Microsoft and Alphabet — deliver updates on AI demand and their capex plans after the bell. Microsoft's report comes just after it offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees as it tries to streamline operations amid the AI build-out.
Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) posted quarterly sales and profit that missed Wall Street expectations.
The Google parent company said revenue, excluding payments to distribution partners, totaled $111.2 billion for the third quarter versus a consensus estimate of $111.3 billion. Earnings per share came to $2.12 a share, compared with the $2.99 forecast by analysts.
The company said its Gemini app has reached 1 billion users.
The company's net income contracted sharply to $26.17 billion, down from $34.90 billion in Q3 2025, despite total revenue climbing 25% to $127.6 billion. Meanwhile, Alphabet's free cash flow deficit widened to $9.06 billion from $5.85 billion in the previous quarter
Microsoft ( MSFT ) stock jumped 4% after the software and cloud giant reported its first quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines.
For the quarter, Microsoft saw earnings per share (EPS) of $4.89 on revenue of $92.28 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $4.73 on revenue of $90.63 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.
Cloud revenue accelerated during the quarter, coming in at $63.9 billion versus Wall Street estimates of $61.62 billion.
US stocks gained on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve voted to hold interest rates steady, with earnings results from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ) looming.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) and the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) each nudged up 0.2% and 0.3%, respectively. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) climbed almost 0.3%
Oracle stock jumped 12% after the software and cloud computing company issued revenue projections of at least $225 billion in fiscal 2030, signaling annualized growth of more than 35%.
Oracle stock jumped 12% after the software and cloud computing giant issued revenue projections of at least $225 billion in fiscal 2030, representing annualized growth of more than 35% from fiscal 2026.
Oracle expects capital spending to peak in fiscal 2027 and 2028, in part to build the capacity needed for its cloud and AI businesses. It expects spending to decline in fiscal 2029.
Oracle expects to reach positive free cash flow during the second half of its fiscal year 2028. The company set a free cash flow target of more than $30 billion for fiscal year 2029.
Though the company is spending heavily now, its projections indicate those investments should translate into substantial cash generation later.
The Fed won't be sitting on its hands for long, says the market.
Traders see about an 85% chance that the Fed raises its benchmark rate by a quarter point at its next meeting on Dec. 9, according to Bloomberg data. The data comes from futures contracts that let traders bet on where the Fed sets rates. Those odds are about where they stood Tuesday, before the decision.
Further out, traders expect the Fed's rate to climb from about 3.9% now to nearly 4.7% by September 2027. That's about three more quarter-point hikes, slightly more than they expected Tuesday.
The Dec. 9 meeting is next. A hike would match what traders already expect. Another hold would mean they've gotten ahead of the Fed.
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh announced a change to the FOMC meeting starting next fall.
Warsh said eight meetings per year is the right number for the Federal Open Market Committee. But in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy with neither a vote on the Fed's funds rate nor a policy statement.
The rest will be regular policy meetings. Warsh also expects that in 2028, policymakers will hold 2 meetings dedicated to strategy and 6 for setting policy.
"Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular, and information-rich intervals," said Warsh.
"But it's equally important we reserve time and space as an intellectually diverse group for strategic deliberations for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons," he added.
The Federal Reserve voted 10-2 on Wednesday to hold interest rates steady in the 3.75% to 4% range following its two-day policy meeting.
Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Fed Governor Lisa Cook dissented, favoring a rate hike.
Markets had widely anticipated the Fed would leave rates unchanged at this meeting, with a potential rate increase at its December meeting.
Investors now await remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, scheduled for 2:30 p.m. ET.
Last Thursday, SpaceX took its worst one-day hit since early August, when its biggest share unlock yet freed up to 1.3 billion shares to trade. Roughly a week later, it's back at the same floor, and the rest of the space trade has left it behind.
SpaceX ( SPCX ) shares were sliding again on Wednesday, along with nearly every space stock.
$140 has been SpaceX's floor since the summer. It marked the top of the stock's August trading range before a breakout, and it sits about halfway between the August low near $108 and the $172 ceiling that capped rallies in June and October.
That makes $140 support , a price where buyers have repeatedly stepped in. They did it twice this month, and the stock is back there again.

articles.title_orig: John Healey tells departments to make 1% cuts to fund defence
articles.title_zh: John Healey tells departments to make 1% cuts to fund defence
articles.content_orig:
Chancellor John Healey has told every government department to find 1% cuts in their capital budgets to fill a £4.7bn hole in the funding of the Defence Investment Plan.
The reductions come on top of the 1% cuts departments were asked to make earlier this year in order to pay for the initial £10.3bn of the plan's overall £15bn price tag.
The plan boosted defence spending; however the chancellor continues to come under pressure to explain how he will meet a further target of spending 3% of national income on defence by 2030.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused the chancellor of only offering "a plan to have a plan" adding:  "I bet [Vladimir] Putin's really scared now."
Setting out his Budget, Healey hinted that meeting that goal would require further cuts, telling MPs it would involve "looking hard at public spending".
He said he would set out how the UK would reach the 3% target by 2030, as well as 3.5% of GDP by 2035, at next year's spending review.
Government departments have yet to decide what will be cut from their capital budgets.
Capital budgets are focused on long-term investments, rather than day-to-day spending. For example, earlier this year, when departments had to make capital budget cuts to fund the initial defence spending rise, a number of major road improvement schemes were scrapped .
Badenoch criticised Healey for not using his Budget to explain how he would boost defence funding to 3%.
"He is the man who is making our country less safe. He has failed his own test. This is on him, and no one will ever forget," she said.
The Conservatives have previously urged the government to pay for defence by making cuts to the welfare budget.
Nato secretary general Mark Rutte said the UK was on "a credible path towards meeting the commitment made by all Nato Allies in The Hague - to ensure we're all investing what's needed to remain ready & able to deter aggression and defend our freedom and security".
Chair of the Commons defence committee - and Labour MP - Tan Dhesi said "some of the key decisions on defence spending have lamentably been delayed until next year's spending review".
He added: "There is a cost to inaction. Investment in our nation's defence and security cannot be kicked into the long grass."
Former Nato secretary general Lord Robertson told the BBC the Budget was "pretty good news for defence generally" but warned there would be "battles ahead with the spending departments" to reach the 3% target.
Earlier this year, Healey resigned as defence secretary, accusing the then-Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer of not providing enough money to keep the UK safe.
In a scathing resignation letter, he specifically emphasised his belief in the importance of reaching a 3% target by 2030.
Now chancellor, Healey told the House of Commons on Wednesday: "At the spending review next year, I confirm that I will set out the details of how we will meet our Nato commitment to spend 3.5% of GDP on defence by 2035, with a target date for 3% in 2030.
"And today, I am getting work under way to get there in a fiscally sustainable way."
In addition to looking at public spending, Healey said he also wanted to use "more innovative financing alongside the private sector and our international allies".
The chancellor said this would include:
The Office for Budget Responsibility estimates that the UK government's target to increase defence spending to 3.5% of GDP by 2035 will cost £35bn.
Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said: "Increasing investment in defence companies may contribute to the target but it is unclear how much this will lead to an increase in UK defence capabilities.
"There is much further to go to get to 3% of GDP on defence and it is hard to believe that this government will want to get there without topping up spending totals."
In his Budget speech, Healey also announced £10bn of economic and military support for Ukraine, in the form of loans and export guarantees.
The funding includes £5.5bn of loans through World Bank guarantees and a grant contribution to the World Bank International Development Association's crisis facility.
A further £3bn will be made available to Ukraine through loans facilitated by UK Export Finance, a government export credit agency.
Healey told the House of Commons that the week had started with Russia launching a "brutal ballistic missile attack" and that the extra money would send "a clear message to Moscow".
He said that when he told the Ukrainian leader about the additional support in a phone call, President Volodymyr Zelensky had said: "You've made my day."
Later on social media, Zelensky welcomed the money, saying: "Every step to strengthen Ukraine brings Russia closer to realising that it must end this war of its own making."
The money comes on top of the UK's pledge to provide Ukraine with £3bn of military support until at least 2030-31.

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas as Qatari mediators say they presented new draft deal to Tehran
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas as Qatari mediators say they presented new draft deal to Tehran
articles.content_orig:
Qatar is awaiting a response from Tehran to a new proposal that could see Iran take a limited step on its nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief and potentially the release of frozen funds, two regional diplomats told The Jerusalem Post . The response could come as early as Thursday.
The measure under consideration would involve allowing inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to return to Iran’s nuclear sites in return for sanctions relief.
On Tuesday, IAEA Director-General Rafael Grossi briefed members of the UN Security Council, saying that only the return of inspectors to the ground could provide an accurate picture of the current state of Iran’s nuclear program.
"I invite Iran to work with the IAEA without any further delay to clarify outstanding safeguards questions and to give the IAEA the information and access the agency requires, so that it can verify all relevant facilities and material, as is Iran's legal obligation," Grossi said.
The proposal comes amid continued difficulties in negotiations between Washington and Tehran. Iran has demanded that the US lift its blockade and provide some sanctions relief before discussions on its nuclear program can begin. The Trump administration, however, has insisted that Iran take an initial step on the nuclear issue from the outset of any agreement.
The return of IAEA inspectors could offer a potential starting point for bridging the gap between the two sides, while allowing the international community to assess the status of Iran’s nuclear activities.
Senior officials from the mediating countries told Iranian officials that this deal might be "the last chance before President Trump might decide to launch a military operation against Iran ".
“As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait.
"The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections", Anna Kelly, White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary, told the Jerusalem Post. The midterms will be held next Tuesday. Kelly also added that “As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait".

articles.title_orig: Putin hails Elon Musk’s ‘genius’ amid plans for Russian version of Starlink
articles.title_zh: Putin hails Elon Musk’s ‘genius’ amid plans for Russian version of Starlink
articles.content_orig:
Russia plans to build own version of US billionaire’s satellite communications to help attack Ukraine
Vladimir Putin praised Elon Musk’s genius and said he was in touch with Starlink’s controlling shareholder as Russia develops its own satellite communications for its military to use against Ukraine.
The Russian president, speaking at a summit with African leaders in Moscow, was comparing the Earth-orbiting network built by Musk’s SpaceX with Russia’s gradual efforts to build its own Rassvet constellation.
“Elon Musk is a genius, a true genius,” the Russian leader said, according to the Tass news agency. “How many of these [satellites] does he have in orbit? More than 5,000, and we’re only taking the first steps.”
The true number of active SpaceX satellites is estimated at about 10,000, which provide the high-speed internet service that has been the subject of a diplomatic row between Musk, the US and Ukraine earlier this month.
A military version of Starlink, called Starshield, was suddenly restricted one night in the middle of October, preventing Ukraine from conducting medium drone attacks and hampering some of its anti-drone air defences.
Initially, Musk, an ally of the US president, Donald Trump, denied that he had ordered a throttling of the internet connection, before saying at the end of last week that he had closed a loophole in which the civilian Starlink had been used by the military.
Putin appeared to be trying to flatter Musk, whose control of the communications technology has raised questions about the US billionaire’s leverage over the White House and the impact he is able to have on Ukraine’s war effort.
“We are in close contact with our American partners – including Mr Musk – because it is very important, in orbit, not to get in each other’s way and ​to maintain a certain level of discipline and order,” Putin said.
Starlink does not work in Russia and its use by Russia inside Ukraine was restricted earlier this year. Meanwhile, Moscow has begun to develop an alternative system, though, with an estimated 26 working satellites, its capacity is limited.
Last week, after about 10 days of restriction, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , announced that “Starlink and Starshield operations have been restored” and that the speeds were “now where they need to be”.
Few believe the issue is permanently settled, with relations between Zelenskyy and Trump fraught in the run-up to the US midterm elections next Tuesday. Trump has also reached out to Putin, agreeing to buy diesel from Moscow early in October in an effort to reduce the oil price before Americans go to the polls.
Zelenskyy said on Wednesday that he hoped proposed trilateral peace talks, involving Ukraine, Russia and the US, would take place between 6 and 10 November in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the UAE, shortly after the midterms.
“We are waiting for the American side. I think that they’ll be ready with all the answers after the elections,” the Ukrainian leader said at a press conference in The Hague with the Dutch prime minister, Rob Jetten.
after newsletter promotion
Earlier, Zelenskyy said he had spoken to Andy Burnham, the UK prime minister, as it emerged that Britain would provide £10bn in extra financing for Ukraine over the next three years – and an immediate £500m for air defence systems.
The additional aid was, Zelenskyy said, “a truly strong and very timely step” that came “as Russia needs to see and feel that Ukraine will not be left alone” as the war heads towards what is expected to be its most difficult winter yet.
John Healey, the UK chancellor, announced the extra funding as part of the government’s annual budget. “The prime minister and I called President Zelenskyy to tell him about our commitments in the budget today. He told us: ‘You’ve made my day’.”
The Dutch government also said it would provide €500m in military support for the winter, and a further €1.2bn in non-military aid, partly to help fund urgent repairs to Ukraine’s utilities and manufacturing.
Kyiv has been relentlessly attacked by Moscow this autumn as Russian forces fail to make progress on the frontlines in the east of Ukraine.
Russia had launched more than 100 ballistic missiles against Kyiv and the surrounding region since the middle of October, Zelenskyy said overnight, hitting power plants and other key targets in an effort to cause a humanitarian crisis in the capital.

articles.title_orig: Residents on the doomed Villa Vie Odyssey cruise describe the first 24 hours after being kicked off in Cambodia
articles.title_zh: Residents on the doomed Villa Vie Odyssey cruise describe the first 24 hours after being kicked off in Cambodia
articles.content_orig:
Passengers on a live-aboard round-the-world cruise say they were abruptly asked to leave the ship and given only hours to disembark.
Villa Vie Residences, which operates the residential cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey , said on Tuesday it had halted operations due to surging fuel costs.
The ship was docked at the port of Sihanoukville in Cambodia when the announcement was made, with passengers saying they were given only eight hours to disembark.
"On October 27, 2026, we received notice from the CEO at around 6 a.m. that all residents had to disembark by 2 p.m. that day," passengers Lanette Canen and John Bodin told Business Insider by email.
Canen and Bodin have been on the Odyssey since it first set sail in September 2024 and run a YouTube channel called Living Life on a Cruise about their experiences on board.
"We knew leaving was a possibility, but the eight-hour notice still surprised us," they said.
The couple shared a video on their YouTube channel that appears to show the moment a staff member announced that passengers must leave the ship.
"Unfortunately, they were unable to secure the fuel necessary to continue operations," a male voice says in the video.
A notice on the Villa Vie Residences website says the company is working with residents to arrange temporary living arrangements and that it is evaluating restructuring options over the next 60 days.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Villa Vie Residences did not immediately respond to requests for comment. CEO Kathy Villalba and executive chairman Mikael Petterson did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Villa Vie Residences said in a statement on Tuesday that the surging cost of fuel since the beginning of the Iran war had made operating the cruise liner increasingly difficult.
The company said its monthly fuel expenses per cabin, which had previously averaged about $1,800, had risen as much as 344% in parts of Asia, to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000.
"Since the conflict began in late February, we have taken significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port," Villa Vie Residences said.
"Those measures have not been enough to offset the extraordinary increase in fuel costs, and we have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses."
On August 1, Villalba, the CEO, sent residents a message titled "Urgent operational update" on an internal messaging platform. In the message, she referenced a "fuel contribution" that had been previously requested of residents. Business Insider has viewed a screenshot of the message.
"When the fuel contribution was requested several months ago, participation was not universal," she wrote in the message. "The contributions received helped some, but they covered only part of the extraordinary increase in fuel costs."
Villalba wrote that the "cash-flow" challenge had continued, and the Odyssey needed 650 metric tons of fuel, adding that fuel prices had almost doubled.
"We have now reached a critical point. The lack of full participation, combined with the unprecedented increase in fuel costs, means we must make immediate and creative operational decisions to preserve the voyage," her message said.
It continued, "We are asking every Resident who did not previously contribute to please do so now. We are also asking those who are able to provide additional support to consider helping with this immediate fuel requirement."
Villalba described the financial need as "real, immediate, and necessary to keep Odyssey moving." It went on, "This is a moment when preserving our home and continuing the voyage requires support beyond contractual minimums from those who are able to provide it."
Among the passengers asked to disembark on Tuesday with only a few hours' notice was Barbara Fiegel, 62, who has lived with her partner aboard the ship since December 2024.
"Everybody's just shocked, everybody's just saddened by this whole issue," she said. "We're still processing, trying to debate what we're going to do."
Fiegel said she and her partner booked a hotel room in Cambodia, then returned to the ship Tuesday evening and Wednesday afternoon to empty their safe and pack their belongings. "Today, as we approached, as we went back on the shuttle back to the ship, I couldn't stop crying," she said.
They plan to return on Thursday to collect their remaining items. Fiegel described the atmosphere on the Odyssey as a “ghost town.”
Joel Greiff, 57, moved aboard the ship at the start of the month. “I was planning to live on the ship for 10, 20, or 73 years,” he said. “I don’t think that will be happening.”
When residents were told to disembark, Greiff emptied his cabin. “I personally grabbed everything,” he said.
He said he would like to return if Villa Vie Residences resumes operations. If not, he is planning to move to Thailand. In the meantime, he has rented an apartment in Cambodia for a month.
Greiff said he plans to return to the Odyssey on Thursday to assist other residents and “help with their luggage, help them find a place, and just start getting them and all their stuff off the ship.”
Have you spent any time on the Villa Vie Odyssey as a cabin owner, renter, or staff member? If you have a story to share, get in touch with this reporter: jzitser@businessinsider.com .

articles.title_orig: Apple Releases Redesigned Mac Chargers and 'World Travel Adapter Kit'
articles.title_zh: Apple Releases Redesigned Mac Chargers and 'World Travel Adapter Kit'
articles.content_orig:
Apple today began selling updated versions of its 70W Power Adapter , 140W Power Adapter , and Power Adapter Extension Cable , all with a new "AC Connector 2."
The updated power adapters and extension cable are available on Apple's online store in the U.S. and many other countries around the world.
Apple also released an updated version of its World Travel Adapter Kit that had disappeared from its online store in 2025, with U.S. pricing set at $39. Each of the international AC plugs included in the box now have the AC Connector 2 too.
Apple's power adapters have a removable plug, and the World Travel Adapter Kit contains various plug types for international travel:
The kit includes five interchangeable AC plugs: Type A: North America, Japan Type C: Continental Europe, Brazil Type D: India Type G: United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Singapore Type I: Australia, New Zealand
In a new support document , Apple said its updated power adapters, extension cable, and plugs use the AC Connector 2 with a pill-shaped design to comply with "updated regulations." Apple's previous "AC Connector 1" has a notched design.

articles.title_orig: Lula’s Election Win in Brazil Is a Relief for China - The Diplomat
articles.title_zh: Lula’s Election Win in Brazil Is a Relief for China - The Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a signing ceremony at the Great Hall of the People, Beijing, May 13, 2025.
On October 4, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva finished the first round of Brazil’s presidential election behind his main rival, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro and an open ally of U.S. President Donald Trump. Flavio Bolsonaro had taken 47 percent of valid votes against Lula’s 45 percent. Because no one topped 50 percent of votes, however, the race went to a second-round runoff.
The first post-election poll gave Bolsonaro a six-point lead in the head-to-head contest. Three weeks later, Lula won with 51.76 percent , a margin of roughly 4.3 million ballots, securing an unprecedented fourth term. His victory came after intense popular demonstrations in leading cities such as Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Belo Horizonte, as well as a new social media strategy boosted by political allies.
Lula’s comeback matters well beyond Brasília. Since late 2025, Latin America has seen a regional shift toward right-wing regimes. Bolivia, Chile, Honduras, Costa Rica, Colombia, and Peru all elected conservative governments, most of them endorsed by Washington.
Brazil was meant to be the crowning piece of Trump’s foreign policy, seeing as it is the largest market in the region and one of the only ones who did not agree on Trump’s Shield for the Americas initiative . Instead, Brazil has opted for a pragmatic foreign economic policy, trying to negotiate with both China and the United States.
The Donroe Doctrine Meets Its Limits
Washington’s strategy has been referred to as the “Donroe Doctrine,” claiming the United States’ right to assert its interests in the region in security terms. In practice that has meant rewarding ideological allies and treating Chinese influence as a central opposing force.
A series of electoral victories seemed to confirm the effectiveness of Trump’s approach to the region. Rodrigo Paz ended two decades of Movimiento al Socialismo (MAS) rule in Bolivia in October 2025. José Antonio Kast won Chile in December. Nasry Asfura took office in Honduras after Trump threatened to cut aid if he lost. In June 2026, Colombia elected the Trump-endorsed outsider Abelardo de la Espriella , and Keiko Fujimori finally won Peru on her fourth attempt. Moreover, Argentina’s right-wing President Javier Milei continues to be an ally.
Tensions between Brazil and the United States have been accumulating in Trump’s second term. In July 2025, the U.S. president imposed tariffs of up to 50 percent on Brazilian goods over the prosecution and later incarceration of Jair Bolsonaro and sanctioned the Supreme Court judge overseeing the case.
On May 26, 2026, Trump received Flavio in the Oval Office, and on June 2, a day after his administration proposed a fresh 25 percent tariff on Brazilian goods, Trump praised him publicly . Flavio asked Washington to postpone the tariffs until after the voting period, but it was too late: a Datafolha poll found that 52 percent of Brazilians saw the tariffs as an effort to help his campaign, but ultimately hurting the Brazilian economy.
Until 2030, Brazil and Mexico, the two largest economies in Latin America, will be governed by center-left leaders, both of whom refuse to pick a clear side between Washington and Beijing. For a doctrine premised on sorting the hemisphere into aligned and unaligned camps, this is a strategic setback for Trump, precisely at a moment where the leader faces low approval rates at home.
Beijing’s Geoeconomic Influence in the Region Is Growing
For China, Brazil is now a strategic partner. In 2025 it was the single largest destination for Chinese outbound investment worldwide, absorbing 10.9 percent of the total, according to the China-Brazil Business Council (CEBC). Chinese investment in China reached $6.1 billion, up 45 percent, far outpacing both Brazil’s overall foreign direct investment (FDI) growth of 4.8 percent and China’s global outbound growth of 1.3 percent .
Overall Brazil accounts for almost two thirds of China’s FDI in South America, with a total stock of $85.5 billion , distributed across 355 projects, between 2007-2025.
China continues to invest heavily in Brazil’s electricity sector, spanning renewable generation and transmission . Automotive investment rose 66 percent to $965 million as BYD began production at the former Ford complex in Camaçari, Bahia (Northeastern Brazil), and Great Wall Motors at the former Mercedes-Benz plant in Iracemápolis, São Paulo. Geely has sealed an alliance with Renault do Brasil and plans local production in Paraná (Southern Brazil) this year.
Beyond investment, bilateral trade hit a record $171 billion in 2025. China bought nearly 80 percent of Brazil’s soybean exports. These ties survived even Jair Bolsonaro’s hostile rhetoric. But a Flavio government that owed its political capital to Washington would have faced intense pressure to slow Chinese investment, and it would have inherited brand-new legal tools to do so (more on this below).
After his loss, Flavio Bolsonaro immediately fled Brazil, heading secretly to the United States via Argentina, amid fears of being convicted of ties to money laundering schemes.
Brazil and the Race for Technology and Critical Minerals
Lula signed Law 15.506/2026 on September 16, creating Brazil’s first National Policy on Critical and Strategic Minerals (PNMCE) and a council, the CIMCE, attached to the presidency. The stakes for investors are considerable: Brazil holds the world’s second-largest rare earth reserves and leads global niobium production, with newly found lithium and nickel reserves.
China still controls roughly 90 percent of rare earth processing and magnet manufacturing and the United States was seeking to secure privileged access to exploration of this sector in the Brazilian market.
The new law has two main aspects: promotion and regulation. The first key is promotion in an industrial policy style. Brazil’s government will provide up to 7 billion Brazilian real in support for firms aiming to raise production and processing of critical minerals, as well as tax credits of up to 1 billion real a year between 2030 and 2034, tied to value-adding and processing on Brazilian soil.
The second aspect is regulation. The newly formed council, led by the president, must approve direct or indirect changes of control in companies holding rights to critical minerals, as well as international supply agreements that could affect Brazil’s economic or geopolitical security.
On paper, this created a screening mechanism that can be used as a hurdle for Chinese state capital, depending on the elected administration. A senior official at the Ministry of Mines and Energy said in October that scrutiny would concentrate on business groups or financing backed by foreign governments, while purely domestic deals may be exempt.
Today, the most visible foreign investors in Brazilian rare earths are American. In April 2026, USA Rare Earth acquired the Serra Verde Mining Complex , Brazil’s only commercial producer of rare earths, for $2.8 billion, in a deal backed by the U.S. government, including $565 million in direct funding from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation.
Meanwhile, between 2024-2025 three Chinese state-owned enterprises invested more than $1.2 billion in acquisitions of copper, nickel, niobium and lithium mines in Brazil. BYD has held lithium rights in Minas Gerais region since 2023.
Under Lula, the CIMCE is likely to wield screening as an industrial policy filter, asking how much value stays in Brazil. The new law rewards precisely what Chinese firms can offer and Washington struggles to: refining know-how, battery materials capacity, and captive demand from EV plants already operating in Brazil. Under a Flavio government, however, the same powers could easily have been aligned with Washington’s geoeconomic

articles.title_orig: Everything Apple Announced This Week: All About OLED, MacBooks And A Touchscreen
articles.title_zh: Everything Apple Announced This Week: All About OLED, MacBooks And A Touchscreen
articles.content_orig:
In addition to the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display at a "Pro and Tell" event in LA, this week brought us an OLED iPad mini and M6 MBP.
Apple wasn't done with its product reveals for the fall after unveiling the iPhone Duo , iPhone 18 Pro models and an array of smart home devices . Nor could it wait until the third event of the season, dubbed "Pro and Tell," to show off more gear.
The company got a string of announcements underway on Monday with the reveal of the long-awaited OLED iPad mini. Tuesday brought us an M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro. Then, on Wednesday, Apple unveiled its long-anticipated touchscreen MacBook Pro.
Elsewhere, Apple released the latest versions of its operating systems. Among other things, those added more Siri AI features and made the assistant available in more languages. The company updated Apple Creator Studio with more AI features and creative tools as well.
Here's an overview of everything Apple announced this week.
It feels like we've been waiting for forever for Apple to put an OLED display in the iPad mini but that day has finally arrived. The new display has double the peak brightness of the one on the previous model at 1,200 nits, and it has a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The base storage remains the same at 128GB, though if you opt for 256GB or 512GB of storage, you can snag a variant with a nano-texture glass display. That'll cost you extra, naturally.
The company managed to squeeze in a larger screen — an 8.5-inch display rather than the 8.3-inch one in the previous model — without increasing the size of the tablet. In fact, the new iPad mini is slightly narrower than the last one, at 5.22 inches vs. 5.3 inches. It's lighter as well, with the Wi-Fi model coming in at 0.56 pounds (compared with 0.65 pounds last time) and the 5G variant weighing 0.58 pounds (versus 0.66 pounds). The latter, by the way, now boasts Apple's C2 modem, which is said to deliver up to 50 percent faster data speeds than the previous iPad mini. There's also Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity thanks to the N1 chip.
The OLED iPad mini — the eighth generation of the device — runs on the A20 Pro, the same chipset as the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. Apple says the SoC is capable of running large language models locally, in case you're into that kind of thing. Otherwise, the tablet should be notably faster than earlier models. It supports Apple Intelligence and Siri AI as well, of course. The chipset also boasts a 7-core GPU — two more cores than the A17 Pro, which powered the last-gen iPad mini.
On the camera front, there's a 12MP Center Stage lens on front of the tablet, which Apple has finally shifted to the landscape edge on the iPad mini. However, there's still no Face ID. The 12MP camera on the rear supports 4K 60fps video capture and Smart HDR 4.
The 8th-gen iPad mini has a sealed enclosure to help protect it from the elements. The tablet has an IP67 rating, meaning that it should withstand dust and being immersed in a meter of freshwater for up to 30 minutes, though I would advise against intentionally submerging your iPad mini.
As for battery life, Apple says that should be roughly the same as last time. The company says the new iPad mini should run for up to 10 hours when you're watching video or surfing the web over Wi-Fi. That drops down to nine hours if you're browsing over a cellular connection. If you have at least a 35W power adaptor, you'll be able to recharge the battery to 50 percent of its capacity in 30 minutes, Apple says.
The most interesting thing to me about this iPad mini is that it has Apple's first Acoustic Display, which the company says helps it deliver "an even better audio experience." It claims the tablet offers more volume and "punchier bass" thanks to woofers that "are paired through the display." Apple added that "custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs." I'm definitely curious to find out how all of that sounds in practice.
Inevitably, the latest iPad mini comes with a price hike. It starts at $699, which is $150 more than the previous model after Apple increased the price of that in June . Pre-orders are now open and the tablet will hit shelves on November 6.
On Tuesday, Apple gave the iMac and MacBook Pro spec bumps. The desktop and laptop now each have the M6 chipset , which recently debuted in the Mac mini .
Let's start with the new iMac . Apple says the M6's dual 16-core neural engine enables it to deliver up to five times faster on-device AI performance (for Siri AI, Apple Intelligence and local LLMs) than the previous-gen iMac from 2024 , which had the M4 chipset. The M6 is said to deliver up to 1.5 times faster performance than the M4 for daily tasks, up to two times faster graphics performance (for photo editing etc.) and up to two times higher gaming performance with ray tracing.
The base-level M6 has 10 CPU cores (two super, three performance and two efficiency cores) and a 10-core CPU, compared with eight of each in the M4. There's the option to have a 12-core M6, in which case your desktop will have four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of the two that the base model has. The four-port model has a nano-texture glass option as well.
Elsewhere, Apple has introduced its N1 networking chip to the iMac. As such, the computer has support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread connectivity. It also has the option to add a 2.5Gb Ethernet port, an upgrade from gigabit Ethernet on the M4 iMac.
Specs otherwise are the same as last time. You'll still get a 24-inch 4.5K Super Retina display, a 12MP Center Stage camera, a six‑speaker Dolby Atmos system, at least 16GB of RAM and 256GB of base storage. The dimensions are identical too, though the M6 iMac is a touch lighter than the previous gen at 9.7 pounds (versus 9.74 pounds). Don't expect any changes to the color options either — the new iMac is still available in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver.
One other thing that's staying the same? The starting price, at least after the $200 increase that Apple gave the M4 iMac over the summer. The new model starts at $1,499, and the four-port version will run you at least $1,699. Pre-orders are open and you'll be able to pick one up in store on November 6.
The latest 14-inch MacBook Pro has the 12-core version of the M6 chipset and the N1 networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. Those appear to be the only spec changes this time.
Compared with the previous-gen 14-inch MBP, which had an M5 SoC, Apple says the M6 model offers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads. It's said to deliver up to 1.3 faster rendering performance with ray tracing in Blender, up to 1.2 times faster image-processing performance in Affinity and up to 1.3 faster project build performance for compiling code in Xcode.
It doesn't seem like this will be a massive upgrade for folks with an M5 model. However, if you have an older MacBook Pro (or really need those incremental improvements from the previous gen), it might be worth making the switch.
Either way, creatives might want to take note of all the updates that are rolling out for Apple Creative Studio . Apple has given Final Cut Pro a long-awaited quality-of-life upgrade by letting you pull clips from the primary storyline and place them anywhere on the timeline, which seems like very basic functionality to have! MotionVFX is integrated into the app on Mac as well, so you'll have thousands of elements at your fingertips for your video edits.
If you have a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence and is set to US English, Logic Pro has an "intelligent assistant" powered by OpenAI that's available in beta. The app has an an enhanced Stem Splitter that can now separate drums as well. In addition, Keynote, Pages and Numbers now have a chatbot you can use to adjust presentations, documents and spreadsheets.

articles.title_orig: Supreme Court wants to hear from Hillary Clinton before deciding on Trump’s petition
articles.title_zh: Supreme Court wants to hear from Hillary Clinton before deciding on Trump’s petition
articles.content_orig:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday told Hillary Clinton to respond to a petition from President Donald Trump that seeks to revive his lawsuit that claims she conspired with others ahead of the 2016 election to “weave a false narrative” that his campaign colluded with Russia .
Lower courts have rejected Trump’s suit, and he wants the justices to intervene. Clinton and her civil co-defendants initially waived their right to respond to Trump’s petition. Had the court not requested a response, that would have all but guaranteed that the petition was headed for denial.
Although the response request is good news for Trump, it doesn’t necessarily signal the court is certain to grant review of his petition. Because it takes only one justice to request a response, it’s unclear how much of an appetite there is on the nine-member bench to take this one up. Response requests don’t specify how many justices asked for the response, nor do they explain why the response was requested.
It takes four justices to grant review.
Clinton’s brief opposing Trump’s petition is now due Nov. 27. The justices will consider in a private conference at some point after that whether to grant review. The Democrat recently made news for endorsing expanding the number of justices who sit on the court that currently has a 6-3 majority of Republican appointees.
Trump argues that he put off bringing the civil case during his first term due to his presidential responsibilities at the time. In his petition , his personal lawyers cast high court review as “necessary to protect the Presidency, and to prevent judicial disagreement from becoming a license to punish its advocates.”
The lower courts have rejected Trump so far. A conservative appeals court upheld a district judge’s ruling that dismissed his suit and imposed nearly $1 million in sanctions against him, Alina Habba and her law firm. The appellate panel noted that many of his and Habba’s legal claims “were indeed frivolous.”
The panel also cited the Supreme Court’s 1997 ruling in Clinton v. Jones that said Bill Clinton couldn’t avoid judicial process in civil litigation while he was in office. “If a president can be haled into court, he cannot be excused from suing to enforce his rights,” the panel reasoned.
In his Supreme Court petition, Trump’s lawyers maintained that there is an important distinction between suing and being sued. They said the Clinton v. Jones precedent “permitted another citizen’s suit against the President while requiring respect for the Presidency; it did not require him to pursue his own claims while in office or lose them.”
They also cited the Supreme Court’s 2024 criminal immunity ruling in Trump’s favor to argue that courts can’t make presidents decide whether to initiate personal litigation while in office. His lawyers are pressing that position as the president pursues an array of personal litigation , including multiple defamation claims .
This case is not Trump’s only pending bid to persuade the justices to revive personal litigation that he has lost in lower courts, nor is it the only one to invoke the presidency in doing so.
Although the Supreme Court has already rejected one of his two petitions seeking to reverse his defamation losses against the writer E. Jean Carroll, his second petition is awaiting a response from Carroll before the justices decide whether to grant or likewise deny that one. There, too, his lawyers cite the criminal immunity ruling in seeking to overturn the $83.3 million judgment Carroll won for statements Trump made during his first term.
The president is also pressing a defamation appeal against CNN over the network’s use of the phrase “big lie” regarding his 2020 election claims. That petition is awaiting a response from CNN, which, as happened in this Clinton litigation, the court requested after the network waived its right to respond.

articles.title_orig: China-Vatican deal has imperfections, Vatican’s foreign minister says
articles.title_zh: China-Vatican deal has imperfections, Vatican’s foreign minister says
articles.content_orig:
Archbishop Paul Gallagher acknowledged the agreement’s challenges in a meeting with journalists in Rome.
Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Vatican’s secretary for relations with states and international organizations, acknowledged the challenges of the Vatican-China deal on Tuesday.
Speaking at an event with journalists in Rome, the British diplomat responded to questions regarding the agreement, Pope Leo XIV’s health, and calls for a ceasefire in the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian war.
The full text of the 2018 agreement between China and the Holy See has never been made public. Under the publicly understood terms of the agreement, the pope retains final authority over episcopal appointments in China and may reject candidates proposed by Beijing. The Holy See, for its part, agreed not to appoint bishops without the Chinese government’s prior approval.
As reported by Reuters , Gallagher said that, regarding the agreement, its imperfections were visible.
“Itʼs not easy, the dialogue is not easy,” Gallagher said. “The imperfections of the agreement are ⁠evident, but ​there is a commitment to persevere in dialogue ... and that is what will ​continue to happen.”
He also answered questions regarding a potential visit from Leo to the U.S., saying that it could happen “in the not too distant future.”
Regarding the pope’s Oct. 13 surgery and subsequent recovery, Gallagher described it as a “bit of a game changer” and a revelation of the pope’s mortality, as with every human being.
“[The pope] is a poor mortal like the rest of ​us,” Gallagher said.
In August, Gallagher traveled to Russia to discuss the country’s ongoing war with Ukraine with senior officials. He told journalists that he did not believe the Vatican was involved in discussions of the ceasefire between the two nations.

articles.title_orig: Google adding more Connected Apps to Gemini & Search with new dev platform
articles.title_zh: Google adding more Connected Apps to Gemini & Search with new dev platform
articles.content_orig:
Google today announced the Connected Apps Platform as a “unified way for more app developers to bring their capabilities directly into Gemini and Search.”
Existing third-party Connected Apps let you access Adobe, Dropbox, Instacart, OpenTable, Ticketmaster, and other services — now numbering over 50 — from the Gemini app. Google also announced a new Calm integration that will be available in the coming weeks. These @-integrations join first-party offerings like Google Workspace, Photos, and YouTube. To date, the creation process has required working closely with Google.
Google is now expanding availability on multiple fronts, starting with the Connected Apps Platform. It’s billed as a way to “build once and reach high-intent users.” Developers need to have a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs. They then register, test, and submit their Connected Apps using the new Google Connected Console. This new website lets them track traffic, latency, and error rates, as well as control brand identity.
In addition to the Gemini app, Google will soon make existing Connected Apps available in Search. Developers can “choose whether [their app] will go live in Search, the Gemini app, or both.” As part of the recent redesign, the Gemini app gained a new Customize page .
Developers can sign up for the preview at developers.google.com/connected-apps . Google is opening up access in phases over the coming months.
